  Cultural and historical VIP tours that include Costa Rica differ in their geography. ## Cultural and historical VIP tours to Costa Rica: understanding the selection

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. One important characteristic is that **Costa Rica is part of the journey, but cultural and historical experiences are often spread across neighbouring countries**. One tour introduces travellers to the Emberá community in Panama and colonial Granada in Nicaragua. Another explores Maya history in Guatemala and Honduras, while Costa Rica provides the main nature-focused section.

Decide what you want most: to discover several Central American countries or to concentrate on Costa Rica's own history. For the first option, these ready-made multi-country itineraries provide a useful starting point. For the second, explore our [Costa Rica destination guide](/costa-rica/) and consider adding dedicated museum and heritage stops. A tour's inclusion in a cultural category does not, by itself, confirm a visit to every monument.

**The VIP catalogue does not mean identical service arrangements on every trip.** Transport, excursion format, hotels, guides, meals and the ability to adjust the schedule are determined by the terms of each itinerary. If history is your main interest, you can also browse [cultural and historical tours featuring Costa Rica without the VIP filter](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/costa-rica/).

## Three options lasting 10–13 days: Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua

On the [10-day Panama and Costa Rica tour](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica/), the cultural section covers the old districts of Panama City, the Panama Canal and an introduction to the Emberá people in Chagres National Park. The Costa Rican section visits [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/), [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/), the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). In other words, Panama provides history and community encounters, while Costa Rica offers nature and parks.

The [13-day Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua tour](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/) adds a third country. The Panamanian portion includes the canal, the Emberá people and Barú Volcano. The route then passes through Manuel Antonio, Monteverde and the [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), before visiting Granada in Nicaragua. This is a good option for travellers wishing to experience different cultural traditions and national parks in one journey.

On the [13-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/), the opening stops are [Doka coffee estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), Poás and La Paz, followed by the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), Arenal and Monteverde. In Nicaragua, the journey continues through Granada, Masaya Volcano and Lake Nicaragua. It ends with a stay on the Pacific coast. This option combines coffee culture, Costa Rican nature and the colonial architecture of Nicaragua.

| Itinerary | Main distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Panama and Costa Rica](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica/) | Emberá culture and the canal, followed by nature |
| [Three countries](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/) | Adds colonial Granada |
| [Costa Rica and Nicaragua](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) | Coffee, volcanoes, Granada and the ocean |

The key measure is the number of meaningful sightseeing days in the country you are most interested in. The total tour duration is not the same as the duration of the cultural programme.

## A 12-day VIP tour with a private flight

The [12-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP journey](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) has a particular transport feature: the programme specifies **a private flight from Puntarenas to Nicaragua**. This is one segment of the journey. Other transfers should not automatically be assumed to take place aboard a private aircraft.

In Costa Rica, the route includes Arenal, Caño Negro, [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/), hanging bridges, a chocolate experience and a tour of Doka coffee estate. In Nicaragua, travellers visit Granada, Lake Nicaragua and Masaya Volcano, with free days by Apoyo Lagoon. This format brings together **natural attractions, culinary traditions and colonial history**, but the detailed list of services needs to be read for each day. For a more focused interest in coffee and chocolate, compare the [Costa Rica food and wine VIP tours](/vip/costa-rica/interests/food-and-wine/).

The programme provides grounds for describing a private flight, but VIP status by itself does not confirm the category of every hotel, personal guiding on every excursion or unlimited itinerary changes.

## Five or six countries: Central American archaeology and history

The [19-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-5-countries-19-days/) covers Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica. The historical section begins in Antigua and at Lake Atitlán, then visits Tikal and Quiriguá in Guatemala, Copán in Honduras, and San Andrés and Joya de Cerén in El Salvador. In Nicaragua, travellers explore León, Managua, Masaya and Granada. Costa Rica rounds off the journey with volcanoes, forests and national parks.

The [24-day Best of Central America tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) also includes Panama, combining Maya heritage, colonial towns, volcanic landscapes, rainforests and encounters with local traditions. It suits someone interested in **the history of an entire region**, rather than the sights of a single city.

A longer itinerary allows more monuments to be seen, but involves more travel and border crossings. Compare the actual time allocated to Tikal, Copán, historic city centres and natural areas rather than choosing solely by the number of countries. The Maya archaeological complexes featured on these routes are outside Costa Rica, which is a crucial distinction when selecting a trip.

## Costa Rica's own culture: San José, Guanacaste and Diquís

To explore Costa Rica's own cultural heritage, begin with [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/). The city houses the National Museum of Costa Rica and the Jade Museum, with archaeological collections and art from pre-Columbian societies. They offer two different perspectives on the country's past: one through the broader story of its development, the other through stone, ceramic and jade craftsmanship.

Guanacaste preserves Chorotega traditions, including the pottery of Guaitil and San Vicente de Nicoya. In southern Costa Rica are pre-Columbian settlements featuring the Diquís stone spheres, inscribed by UNESCO in 2014. They represent a distinct archaeological heritage and are unrelated to the Maya sites of Guatemala and Honduras.

These are **independent ideas for a cultural itinerary**, not extra services already included in the VIP journeys listed here. Visiting them would require a separately agreed route and programme. A trip designed around [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) is primarily nature-focused.

## Practical choices: seasons, geography and service

The relatively dry period on Costa Rica's Pacific coast usually falls between December and March; rainfall patterns on the Caribbean side are different. For museum-focused travel in the capital, opening hours and transfer times matter most; for volcanic parks, weather and visibility are crucial. A multi-country journey requires attention to each region's climate rather than relying on the beach holiday season alone.

Before booking a particular tour, it helps to check:

- **Which countries and cities are compulsory stops.** Distinguish historical sites in Panama, Nicaragua, Guatemala and Honduras from those in Costa Rica itself.
- **What is already included.** Review admission tickets, guiding, meals, domestic flights and road transfers in the chosen programme.
- **Where free time is available.** On a multi-country itinerary, a free day may be at a beach or lagoon rather than a museum in the capital.
- **Which aim matters most.** Longer regional routes work well for Maya monuments; Costa Rica's museums and traditions call for a more targeted itinerary.

If personal arrangements and nature experiences are your priorities, compare [all VIP tours to Costa Rica](/vip/costa-rica/). If culture is your main goal, choose by the specific monuments and the time available to explore them.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do all cultural and historical VIP tours take place only in Costa Rica?

No. This selection includes multi-country itineraries. Historical stops may be in Panama, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador, while the Costa Rican section concentrates on national parks and volcanoes.

### Does Costa Rica have sites from pre-Columbian history?

Yes. San José has museums with archaeological collections, and pre-Columbian settlements with the Diquís stone spheres survive in the south. Check the chosen itinerary to confirm whether visits are included.

### Is a private aircraft included in every VIP tour?

No. The [12-day Costa Rica–Nicaragua tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) specifies a private flight for a particular segment. Other itineraries have their own transport arrangements.

### Which route should I choose for Maya monuments?

Compare the [19-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-5-countries-19-days/) with the [24-day six-country journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/). Both include archaeological sites in Guatemala and Honduras.

### Can historical excursions be combined with beach time?

Yes. Some programmes include time on the Pacific coast, though the duration varies. For this priority, browse [Costa Rica beach holiday VIP tours](/vip/costa-rica/interests/beach-holidays/) and check how many free days are provided.

## Which VIP tours with diving are available in Costa Rica?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both programmes devote **a separate day to diving on the Pacific coast**, but differ in itinerary, duration, sea conditions and the demands of their other activities.

| Programme | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Costa Rica Gems, 5 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) | Osa Peninsula, Corcovado and Caño Island; focus on a nature reserve |
| [Extreme Costa Rica, 13 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | Rafting, volcanoes, cloud forest, fishing and a day diving at the Catalina Islands |

The VIP category helps select itineraries within the site's current model, but **does not automatically confirm a private boat, a dedicated dive guide, a personal instructor or a particular hotel category at every stage**. These details must be checked against the individual tour and confirmed in an offer before payment.

If your sole aim is diving with several days at sea, first browse [all Costa Rica diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/). On the current VIP programmes, a single diving day is combined with sightseeing and travel around the country.

## Caño Island: five days for the ocean and Corcovado

On [Costa Rica Gems](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/), the first day is spent in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/). Day two includes a domestic flight to the south of the country, followed by travel along the Sierpe River and through mangrove areas towards the coast of the [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/). Accommodation on this nature-focused part of the itinerary is listed at Rancho Corcovado.

On day three, the trip goes to [Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and Sirena Station. Boarding the boat, landing on the beach and walking with a naturalist along the trails are important parts of this day. It is a nature excursion on land, not a second diving day.

Day four is devoted to [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/). Its marine environment is known for reefs and opportunities to observe fish, rays, turtles and other animals. The species mentioned in the description illustrate the region's diversity, but **sightings of particular animals and underwater visibility are not guaranteed**. A return flight and transfer to the international airport are scheduled for day five.

### What to know about visiting the Caño reserve

[Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) belongs to a protected biological reserve. SINAC sets advance-booking and access rules, requires visitors to be accompanied by a registered, locally certified guide and limits dives to authorised areas. Fishing within the reserve is also prohibited.

For a premium trip, agree in advance **who handles the reservation for the authorised visit**, which company operates the boat, what proof of diving qualification is needed, how many dives can take place that day and whether equipment is included. The VIP label is not a substitute for those confirmations.

The itinerary also features [Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) as part of the journey to Corcovado and the island. This is a good option for travellers wanting to spend most of a short visit in natural surroundings and comfortable with boat transfers, rather than those seeking five days in a single beach hotel.

## Catalina Islands: diving within a longer adventure journey

[Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) lasts 13 days. Before reaching the Pacific, travellers visit [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), go rafting on the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), try canyoning and quad biking near [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and spend an active day in [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/).

The coastal section includes a day of sport fishing near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/), dives around the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) and a free day at the beach. Diving takes place on **day 11**, immediately after the fishing day. The itinerary ends with an airport transfer on day 13.

The description of the diving day explicitly mentions potentially strong currents and challenging surface conditions. The depths of the dive sites vary, with a stated range of **12–35 metres**. The ability to descend quickly and make a safety stop is important, and a drift-diving section is mentioned. This day should therefore be assessed against a participant's actual training and the operator's requirements, not simply as another resort activity.

If the ocean interests you but you have limited diving experience, **the fact that the Catalina Islands are included does not mean you can book the described demanding dive without checking eligibility**. A different programme or a substitute activity would need to be agreed separately before the booking is confirmed.

## How to compare VIP diving arrangements before booking

For the underwater portion of a journey, specific arrangements matter more than broad promises of premium service. Before choosing a programme, check:

- **Dive level and profile.** Is certification required, what is the minimum accepted qualification, how many dives are scheduled and what are the maximum operating depths?
- **Boat and supervision.** Is the excursion shared or private, how many divers does each guide supervise, who conducts the briefing, in which language, and who is responsible for safety?
- **Equipment.** What is covered by the base price, can appropriate sizes be provided, and are a dive computer, safety equipment and extra cylinders included?
- **Logistics.** Where does the boat depart, how long is the journey and what happens if the trip is cancelled because of weather?
- **Permits.** For Caño's protected waters, confirm reservations and access in advance through an operator complying with SINAC rules.

[Caño Island Gems](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) includes domestic flights, a boat and accommodation near Corcovado, while the [13-day itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) involves many more overland transfers and sporting activities. Overall comfort depends on how these stages connect, excursion start times and group arrangements.

Comparing prices solely by the number of days would be misleading. The five-day programme lists a per-person price based on double occupancy; the other programme has its own conditions and inclusions. Consult the current tour pages and their full lists of inclusions and exclusions before dividing the price by the number of nights.

## Flying after diving: an important scheduling detail

When planning dives, leave sufficient time before the next flight. Divers Alert Network provides recommendations for recreational no-decompression diving: **at least 12 hours after a single dive and 18 hours after repetitive dives**. These intervals reduce the risk of decompression sickness but do not guarantee its absence; more complex dive profiles require additional precautions.

In the [five-day programme](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/), diving is scheduled for day four and the return flight for day five. Therefore, **the exact timing of the last dive and the flight should be agreed before purchasing domestic or international tickets**. In the 13-day option, day 12 is free after diving on day 11, and the airport transfer follows on day 13; the actual timing of each stage still needs checking.

The intervals above are general planning information. Decisions on fitness for a particular dive and flight depend on the individual dive profile, health and the professional operator's rules. A recommended surface interval should not be shortened merely to catch a convenient connecting flight.

## When to go and which marine programme to choose

Caño and the Catalina Islands are in different parts of Costa Rica. [Caño](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) lies off the southern coast, while the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) are in the northwest. Conditions vary by area, season, currents and actual weather. Discuss possible dates with the diving programme in mind, including whether the boat day can be rescheduled.

For a short nature-focused trip featuring walks in [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and a separate diving day, the [five-day programme](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) is more convenient. For a fuller itinerary with several sporting activities, consider the [13-day tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), provided the participant is qualified for its marine section.

If you want more time underwater, start with [all diving itineraries in Costa Rica](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/) and discuss a dedicated diving schedule. The current VIP filter does not promise a multi-day liveaboard diving safari.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP diving in Costa Rica

### Which is better: Caño or the Catalina Islands?

In the current Caño itinerary, the marine reserve and the combination with Corcovado are central; the Catalina programme describes currents and drift diving within a long active journey. The right choice depends on experience, available time and interest in the other days.

### Does the VIP price include a private boat?

The published descriptions do not confirm that. If a private departure is needed, request a separate offer specifying vessel type, number of participants, supervision and included equipment.

### Can I join without a diving certificate?

The programmes include diving but do not describe a universal beginner training course. The availability of an introductory experience depends on the rules of the specific dive site and operator. The Catalina description explicitly calls for a higher level of preparation.

### Can diving and fishing be combined?

Yes, they are scheduled on days 10 and 11 of [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/). Fishing is prohibited within the [Caño reserve](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/), so these activities cannot be combined within the same protected waters.

### Is the five-day itinerary suitable for flying home immediately after diving?

Diving is planned for day four, with a flight on day five. Compare the actual times with the appropriate safe interval after the last dive; change the flight or sequence of activities if necessary.

### Where can I find other Costa Rica travel formats?

Compare [nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/), [adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/) and the [full Costa Rica VIP selection](/vip/costa-rica/). They serve different travel priorities.

## What is included in the VIP fishing selection?

This section features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current selection centres on the [13-day Extreme Costa Rica tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/). Its itinerary includes **one full day of offshore sport fishing** near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) on the Pacific coast. That is day 10. After returning, accommodation is planned at Wyndham Tamarindo; breakfast and lunch are listed for this day.

The itinerary was designed to combine different activities. Before reaching the coast, you visit [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) and its canals, go rafting on the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), explore the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and the cloud forest of [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). After the fishing day come diving around the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) and time at the beach. This mix allows a group with varied interests to travel together, but each guest's participation in the active experiences and any alternatives must be agreed separately.

**A VIP catalogue label does not mean that every tour already includes a privately chartered boat, a personal fishing guide or private transfers throughout.** The actual inclusions are stated in the [specific itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/). If a private sea outing matters to you, it needs to be addressed separately in the offer and quotation.

## Fishing near Flamingo: what to expect on the day

[Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) lies in northwestern [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/), on the Pacific coast of Guanacaste. The programme provides for a full-day outing and distinguishes two fishing zones.

**Offshore waters.** About 20 miles west of the port, the water becomes much deeper. The programme lists sailfish, several kinds of marlin, mahi-mahi and tuna among the species found there. This indicates the nature of the fishing, but does not promise a particular species or trophy catch.

**Nearshore waters.** The Catalina and Brummel Islands are considerably closer to shore. The fishing description mentions wahoo, mackerel, horse mackerel, snappers and roosterfish. For guests, the practical differences are time spent travelling offshore, sea conditions, fishing methods and tackle requirements. The captain chooses the precise fishing ground and route according to conditions that day.

Costa Rica's tourism authority identifies Guanacaste as one of the country's main sport-fishing regions. However, seasonal patterns and actual fishing success depend on the species, currents and weather. **Whatever month you choose, discuss your preferred fishing format rather than expecting a guaranteed catch.**

## How to make your fishing day genuinely private

For premium arrangements, agreeing the specifics beforehand is more useful than relying on the word VIP in the category name. Before paying for a programme, ask your travel manager:

- **Boat and group.** Will the vessel be reserved solely for your party or will you join a shared departure? How many guests and anglers will be on board?
- **Route and duration.** Where will you depart, how many hours are set aside for fishing, how long is the journey to distant fishing grounds and what is the alternative plan in strong winds?
- **Equipment.** Which rods, tackle and lures are included, is suitable gear available for a beginner and who provides instruction?
- **Permits and rules.** Who obtains the necessary fishing documents and verifies that the vessel operates legally? What are the procedures for handling and releasing caught fish?
- **Comfort at sea.** What arrangements are made for drinking water, food, sun protection, toilet facilities and assistance with seasickness?

INCOPESCA regulations set specific requirements for recreational sport-fishing documents and vessel permits. **A programme stating “fishing included” does not confirm that every document has already been obtained and paid for.** The applicable permits should be identified explicitly in the booking confirmation.

After a long day at sea, it is sensible to leave time free from other compulsory activities. On [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), the fishing day falls between beach downtime and the diving day. When discussing individual adjustments, keep the schedule realistic and take travellers' wellbeing into account.

## One day of sea fishing or a trip devoted to the ocean?

Ada Tours also offers the [seven-day Costa Rica Fishing programme](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/). It devotes much more of the trip to ocean fishing than the 13-day adventure itinerary. **This specialist tour is not part of the current “Costa Rica + fishing” VIP selection**, so it should not be presented as a second offer under that particular filter. The comparison is nevertheless useful when choosing the right kind of trip.

| Itinerary | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | 13 days: parks, rafting, Arenal, Monteverde, one fishing day and diving |
| [Costa Rica Fishing](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) | 7 days: sea fishing as the main reason for travelling |

If you want several outings targeting different fish species, begin with the [general Costa Rica fishing tour catalogue](/interests/fishing/tours/costa-rica/). To combine the sea, volcanoes and demanding outdoor activities, look at [adventure tours in the country](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/). The difference in travel format matters more than the wording of the category.

## Fishing and diving on one journey

Day 11 of the [13-day itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) is dedicated to diving around the Catalina Islands. The programme is designed for more experienced divers: it describes potentially strong currents, drift sections and dive-site depths reaching 35 metres. The ability to descend and complete a safety stop is explicitly identified as important.

Fishing near Flamingo and diving around Catalina are separate activities. A fishing trip **is not a substitute** for dive training, and taking part does not mean that the following day's dive is suitable for someone with no diving experience. Check the dive operator's qualification requirements before confirming the final order of activities.

Travellers more interested in diving than fishing may prefer the [Costa Rica diving tour selection](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/). It also features a very different location, Caño Island off the Osa Peninsula, with substantially different travel logistics.

## Dates, weather and safety at sea

Weather along the Pacific coast changes over the year, and sea conditions can differ even from one day to the next. Decide in advance whether your priority is maximum time on the boat, a comfortable coastal route or the chance to encounter particular large fish. If the sea is rough or visibility is limited, the licensed operator decides whether to depart and where to fish based on actual conditions.

Bring sun protection and clothing that can get wet, and discuss susceptibility to seasickness before departure. Travellers with health limitations, especially on longer offshore journeys, need to consider the facilities of the particular boat and the option to skip certain activities. Expensive accommodation alone does not address these needs.

For a longer trip around Costa Rica, also check the means of transport and accommodation category at every stop. The terms of the 13-day programme, including meals on particular days and expenses not included, are listed on the [tour page](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about VIP fishing in Costa Rica

### How many fishing days are included in the VIP itinerary?

On the published Extreme Costa Rica programme, day 10 is devoted to sport fishing near Flamingo. The remaining days cover nature excursions, rafting, diving and relaxation. Additional fishing outings require a separate arrangement.

### Will the boat be exclusively ours?

The current description does not confirm exclusive use of the vessel. When booking, request the group size, vessel type and terms for a private charter if you need one.

### Can diving be replaced with another fishing day?

You can discuss changes to the order or selection of activities with Ada Tours, but the published price and itinerary do not confirm such an adjustment. Any revised quotation, boat arrangements and available dates must be agreed before payment.

### Is the trip suitable for someone trying sea fishing for the first time?

The fishing day can be assessed separately from the more demanding parts of the journey. However, the 13-day itinerary also features rafting, canyoning and diving with specific requirements, so discuss the overall physical demands and alternative activities in advance.

### Must caught fish always be released?

That depends on the species, permit type, operator rules and current INCOPESCA requirements. Catch-and-release applies to certain kinds of sport fishing. Confirm the rules for your particular outing before booking.

### Where can I see all fishing programmes, including non-VIP trips?

The [Costa Rica fishing tour catalogue](/interests/fishing/tours/costa-rica/) includes themed journeys in different formats. The [country's VIP selection](/vip/costa-rica/) is broader and is not limited to fishing.

## Which food and wine VIP tours in Costa Rica should you choose?

The central culinary experience on both trips is **a visit to [Doka coffee estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/)**. Here you can follow coffee production from the fruit to processed and roasted beans. It helps reveal how visiting a working estate differs from tasting coffee in a café.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. They cater to different goals. The [12-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) combines coffee and cacao experiences with nature itineraries and a continuation into the neighbouring country. The [eight-day Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/) offers a more compact introduction to one country: a coffee plantation, volcanoes, wildlife observation and the Pacific shore.

## Doka estate: where to discover Costa Rican coffee

[Doka](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/) is in the Sabanilla area of Alajuela Province. A visit can be combined with [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and La Paz Waterfalls. Both journeys do exactly this: coffee becomes the opening part of a substantial sightseeing day before the route continues to natural attractions.

At the estate, travellers learn how coffee plants are grown, cherries harvested, pulp separated, and beans processed and roasted. The 12-day VIP tour explicitly includes a tasting of the finished drink. The eight-day programme confirms a demonstration of the production process, but that description alone does not support a separate promise of a tasting or personal cupping session.

Why is a coffee estate interesting even to someone who drinks coffee every day? In Costa Rica, flavour is linked to elevation, microclimate, the ripeness of the cherries and processing methods. The country's coffee institute, ICAFE, identifies eight coffee-growing regions. The Central Valley, where coffee cultivation first spread, is associated with volcanic soils and distinct wet and drier seasons. At a working farm, these factors become tangible stages of cultivation and processing.

Harvesting and processing are seasonal. Visitors may see different activities depending on the timing of their visit; seeing the harvest actually taking place on a specific day requires separate confirmation. To discover more journeys of this kind, see the [coffee tour selection](/interests/coffee-tours/). The [Costa Rica food and wine tour catalogue](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/costa-rica/) also features programmes beyond the VIP segment.

## A chocolate tour near Arenal: what the 12-day itinerary includes

On the [Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP programme](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/), the chocolate excursion takes place during the stay in the [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). Guests are shown cacao cultivation, fruit harvesting, bean drying and grinding, as well as the preparation of hot chocolate.

The coffee and chocolate excursions offer different insights. At the coffee estate, the focus is on cultivation, bean processing and roasting. At the cacao plantation, visitors can follow the transformation of a tropical tree's fruit into a familiar chocolate product. Together, the excursions reveal two important agricultural crops of Central America.

The chocolate activity is included specifically in the 12-day itinerary. It does not appear in the description of [Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/). It should not automatically be treated as included simply because both journeys feature in the same food and wine selection.

## Combining coffee excursions with Costa Rican nature

Culinary stops make particular sense when they fit naturally into the wider geography of a journey. Both routes continue into mountainous regions after Doka. [Poás](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) offers a volcanic landscape, while near [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) travellers encounter rainforest and hot springs.

Both journeys visit [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) for a boat-based excursion to observe birds and other wildlife. After that, the itineraries diverge:

- The [12-day VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) passes through Río Celeste, then flies to Nicaragua, where visits to colonial Granada and Masaya Volcano are followed by relaxation beside Apoyo Lagoon.
- The [eight-day Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/) stays within Costa Rica, continuing to [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and Marino Ballena National Park on the Pacific coast.

If you want more time in one country and a seaside finale, choose the second option. If chocolate, a second country and a lagoon retreat after an active week appeal to you, the first itinerary is a better match.

## What VIP actually means on these programmes

The title of the [12-day journey](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) mentions a private aircraft: the flight from Costa Rica to Nicaragua is indeed part of its described route. That is a specific feature of this product. [Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/) includes individual ground transport and programme transfers, guiding services, admission tickets and accommodation. A private plane is not listed there.

At the same time, a place in the VIP catalogue does not automatically mean exclusive access to a plantation, a personal coffee expert, a special dinner, a five-star hotel or a tasting of rare varieties. Price inclusions differ, so examine the arrangements for meals and additional excursions particularly closely.

The two trips' prices cannot meaningfully be compared by number of days alone without looking at the pricing basis and included services. Current offers, where comparable figures are available, appear directly on the tour pages. For planning, it is more useful to decide on your preferred destinations and essential experiences first, then discuss guiding and accommodation formats.

## Practical questions about food-focused journeys

### Can I visit Doka estate on both tours?

Yes. It is included in both confirmed itineraries. You can find more about the estate and its location on the [Doka estate page](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/).

### Which programme includes learning about cacao and making chocolate?

The [12-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/). The chocolate excursion takes place near La Fortuna. The eight-day programme only confirms a visit to the coffee farm.

### Can I visit during the coffee-cherry harvest?

The harvest season varies with elevation and weather. The tours explain coffee cultivation and processing, but neither programme promises that guests will see live cherry-picking on a particular day. Keep this in mind when choosing your travel dates.

### Do all food and wine VIP tours to Costa Rica include a private aircraft?

No. The private flight is confirmed separately for the 12-day itinerary continuing to Nicaragua. The eight-day journey stays within Costa Rica and uses road transfers.

### How should I choose between eight and twelve days?

Consider whether you want a second country, a dedicated chocolate excursion, and whether you prefer an ocean finale or time beside a freshwater lagoon. [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and the coast are important parts of the eight-day tour; Nicaragua and the combination of coffee and cacao distinguish the 12-day option.

## Costa Rica VIP nature tours: how to choose beyond a list of beautiful places

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a nature focus and Costa Rica as a main country on the itinerary. Some journeys allow several days in forests and on the ocean shore; others combine two or three nature regions with neighbouring Central American countries. **Choose according to time actually spent at natural attractions, not the number of parks named in a description.**

For volcanoes, consider an itinerary through [Poás](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). For walks in humid forest, [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and Tortuguero are of particular interest. Travellers wanting remote forest areas and coastline should examine longer journeys that explicitly include [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/).

These options differ in transport, conditions and physical demands. Our VIP selection includes programmes with varied arrangements, so private guiding, exclusive transport or a particular hotel must be confirmed in the description of the relevant tour.

## Volcanoes: Arenal and Poás offer different experiences

[Arenal and the La Fortuna area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) are valued for volcanic scenery, forest walks, waterfalls and hot springs. Hanging bridges and hikes along trails may be included. Actual activities vary between tours: one emphasises relaxed nature observation while another features more strenuous pursuits.

[Poás](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) is a volcano known for its crater and high-altitude landscapes. In [Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/), the visit is combined with Doka coffee estate and [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/). The combination is well suited to a full but geographically coherent day without the need to cross half the country between stops.

When choosing volcanic excursions, consider trail conditions, access to craters and visibility in the prevailing weather. A volcano appearing on the itinerary does not mean you can approach any point, see lava or count on an unobstructed panorama. A closure ordered by local authorities can change the entire plan for that sightseeing day.

## Tortuguero, Monteverde and Corcovado: why the forest regions are different

Tortuguero lies on Costa Rica's Caribbean side. Its natural experiences centre on river canals and humid lowland forests. In [Best of Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/best-of-costa-rica/), the journey includes a road transfer to a landing stage followed by a boat trip, a visit to the village and time exploring the forest. Boat access and walking should be treated as separate parts of the journey.

[Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) is a mountain cloud forest, often misty and cooler than the coast. Trails, bridges, botanical observation and visits into the forest take time in addition to the transfer. It is an appealing destination for birdwatching and nature photography, but encounters with particular animals depend on the season, weather and chance.

[Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) is on the Osa Peninsula. It is one of the more demanding stops to organise on a long itinerary: visiting the protected area requires reservations through the national park system and compliance with access rules. SINAC specifies advance reservations, and routes are limited to authorised trails and sectors. An improvised attempt to “drop in for a couple of hours” may therefore be impractical.

The [16-day premium tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) combines Tortuguero, Arenal, Monteverde and Corcovado in one programme. It offers a greater variety of natural regions but requires time to travel between the Caribbean side, the highlands and the Pacific coast.

## When the VIP format really changes the journey

For some travellers, comfort means changing hotels less often; for others, it means private transport on long sections or an individually agreed pace. Check these features on the actual tour page instead of inferring them from the section title. The [16-day Costa Rica itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/), for example, is offered in a private format.

Another confirmed format is the [VIP Costa Rica and Nicaragua tour with a private aircraft](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/). Its principal feature is the stated combination of two countries, volcanic regions and a flight. This is a very different travel experience from an itinerary that devotes most of its time to forest walks and staying in one region.

Compare more than the list of included excursions. Private transport does not eliminate the physical distance between parks, and high-end accommodation does not remove humidity, changes in altitude, boat transfers or restrictions on access to protected areas.

## Choosing the season for forests, volcanoes and the coast

Costa Rica's climate varies between the Caribbean and Pacific coasts and the slopes of its highland ranges. There is no simple “ideal month for the entire country” for a long route taking in both sides of the mountains. Rain and mist may be present in the cloud forest when the beach is sunny, and views of volcanoes often depend on cloud cover.

For journeys through several regions, pack light clothing for hot weather, rain protection, enclosed shoes for trails and layers for cooler mountain evenings. At [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), SINAC regulates conservation rules and entrance tickets, so individual visits need to be confirmed against the national park's current schedule even when the overall trip is planned ahead.

A longer tour through Panama or Nicaragua adds border crossings and further logistics. Check which country is the main destination, where overnight stays are planned and whether the schedule has room for transport changes. Tourist entry requirements depend on citizenship and current regulations, not on the VIP category.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP nature tours

### Does every VIP programme include Corcovado?

No. [Costa Rican Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-treasures/), for example, focuses on other natural attractions, while the [16-day premium itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) includes Corcovado. Its inclusion and visit conditions must be checked against the specific route.

### Are wildlife sightings guaranteed?

No. Wildlife encounters depend on animal behaviour, weather and conservation regulations. Feeding or pursuing animals independently in national parks is not permitted.

### Which is better for a first visit: Arenal or Tortuguero?

Arenal is well suited to volcanic landscapes, walks and thermal areas; Tortuguero is known for its canals and humid lowland forest. [Best of Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/best-of-costa-rica/) includes both on one journey, but travel between the regions is necessary.

### Does VIP mean excursions are always private?

No. Group formats and arrangements differ between programmes. Private transport or personal guiding are confirmed only by the terms of the individual tour.
